scanner_frame_classes.na_to_peer_ns: a Neighbor Advertisement of the scanner's address answering a Neighbor Solicitation of the peer for it: the scanner namespace kernel, and on rmasscan's step its NS responder (T4)
scanner_frame_classes.next_hop_ns: rmasscan's IPv6 next-hop resolution (R11): the Neighbor Solicitation of its resolver for the router fe80::aa:ff:fe00:2 (is_next_hop_ns), only in a case without --router-mac-ipv6
scanner_frame_classes.next_hop_who_has: the IPv4 next-hop resolution of a scan with IPv4 targets: an ARP who-has 198.18.0.2 from 198.18.0.1, 60 bytes zero-padded (the resolver form of C stack-arpv4.c and rmasscan)
scanner_frame_classes.rst_to_rst: C's own TCP RST (no other flag) from the scanner's address of the family whose sequence number is the acknowledgment of an RST of the stand (a closed port): C resets each distinct reply that passes its cookie check and dedup, the RST as well as the SYN-ACK (main.c:1048-1101, `TCP_IS_SYNACK || TCP_IS_RST`, then tcp_send_RST; live 7b r1), in its template's form (window 1200, the MSS option); only on the oracle's step: rmasscan has no RST path and no kernel answers an RST
scanner_frame_classes.rst_to_syn_ack: a TCP RST (no other flag) from the scanner's address of the family whose sequence number is the acknowledgment of a SYN-ACK of the stand: the scanner namespace kernel resets a SYN-ACK no socket owns, and C resets each distinct SYN-ACK itself once it passed its dedup (main.c:1067-1068, :1095; tcp_send_RST builds IPv6 too)

stand_noise_classes.dad_ns: a Neighbor Solicitation from :: (Duplicate Address Detection) from either MAC: the stand sets accept_dad=0 and adds its addresses nodad
stand_noise_classes.mld: an MLD query, report or done (ICMPv6 130, 131, 132, 143) from either MAC: a host reports only when it joins or leaves a group; the stand's groups are joined when it is raised, before wire-lab.sh's settle wait (an unsolicited report is expected to repeat within mldv2_unsolicited_report_interval, 1 s), so none may fall into a step
stand_noise_classes.peer_ns_for_scanner: a Neighbor Solicitation of the peer for the scanner's address: the peer has fd00:198:18::1 as a permanent neighbour, so it never resolves the scanner
stand_noise_classes.router_advertisement: ICMPv6 134: no router daemon runs on the stand and both ends have forwarding=0
stand_noise_classes.router_solicitation: ICMPv6 133 from either MAC: the stand sets accept_ra=0 and router_solicitations=0 on both veth ends
stand_noise_classes.scanner_ns_for_peer: a Neighbor Solicitation of the scanner MAC for a peer's ULA fd00:198:18::2-5: the scanner namespace kernel resolving a peer before it resets a SYN-ACK; the scanner has the peers as permanent neighbours, which prevents it.
